metadata.rules_text:
- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 2–5% to counteract pessimism bias.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast by 3–8% in next 3–5 days to avoid overreaction.
- If model forecast is significantly below recent 10-day moving average (e.g., < 90% of MA), consider mean reversion bias — increase forecast toward MA by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive (e.g., >0.4 in 2–3 days), model often lags; add 1–3% buffer to forecast to capture sentiment momentum.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently underestimates true volatility; apply 1–2% upward adjustment if sentiment is neutral or positive, especially if recent price action shows upward momentum.
- If sentiment is mixed or volatile (±0.3–0.5), model tends to over-smooth; use 1–2% volatility buffer in forecast to reflect uncertainty.
